summary: Preinstall hook downloads Bun runtime and executes a 727 KB obfuscated bundle unrelated to the package's stated purpose
details: The package advertises itself as a Vue UI component library but ships an install-time dropper. package.json declares `preinstall: node setup.mjs`. setup.mjs is itself obfuscated (hex-mangled identifiers such as `_0x488df8`, `_0x52943e` and string-array indirection maps that hide `fs`, `https`, `execFileSync`, and the target URL). At install time it detects platform and libc (musl vs glibc via `ldd`/`/etc/os-release`), downloads the Bun runtime archive from `https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/<platform>.zip` into a temp directory, extracts it (via system unzip, PowerShell Expand-Archive, or an inline ZIP parser), chmods the binary, and invokes it against a sibling file `math_init.js` in the tarball root. math_init.js is a 727 KB Bun-compiled bundle (`// @bun @bun-cjs`) heavily obfuscated with a rotated string array (`WV8StW`/`n7gIxM`) and a decoder function (`hc1jfK9`). math_init.js is not referenced by package.json's `main`, is not part of the declared Vue component surface, and its contents are not human-readable. The combination of an obfuscated preinstall script, an alternate-runtime fetch used to evade Node-focused tooling, and an opaque 727 KB payload executed automatically on `npm install` fires attacker-controlled code on the installer's machine before any consumer code runs.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
